newsitem.title: USA: USDA says average CRP rent will be $39 per acre.
newsitem.headline: USDA says average CRP rent will be $39 per acre.

text.p: The average cost of rental fees paid to farmers for newly-enrolled land in the Conservation Reserve Program will be $39 an acre, Agriculture Department said Thursday.
That compares to an average of about $50 per acre paid in rental fees for land currently enrolled in the program.
"While getting greater environmental benefits, we will be paying 21 percent less per acre -- saving more than $1.6 billion for the life of the program," USDA Secretary Dan Glickman said.
The cost of the newly-enrolled land will be about $1.1 billion annually, or $11.1 billion over the ten-year life of the contracts.

Glickman said the agency had accepted 16.1 million acres in the nation's largest long-term land-idling program, and would hold a second sign-up this autumn. ((Washington commodities desk 202 898 8467))
